statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of four representative page archetypes plus unknown-route recovery.

paths.description: Homepage: primary discovery surface, global navigation, consent/notification entry state and crawler baseline.
Latest Jobs listing: representative long index template and high-volume navigation surface.
UPSSSC OTR detail: representative job/application detail with dense tables and outbound apply journey.
Contact: representative informational/support route and possible input surface.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark-colour preference.
findings.evidence: The dark/reduced-motion screenshot is visually identical to the light capture; the platform probe found zero prefers-color-scheme rules and computed color-scheme: normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and use prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() tokens for surfaces, text, borders and controls.

findings.summary: Two unsolicited prompts obscure the primary content on arrival.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show a full consent wall plus a notification opt-in stacked above it; on 360x800 almost no page content remains operable.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not request notifications on load. Present privacy controls once, compactly, after content is available, and keep rejection as easy as acceptance.

findings.summary: Overlay implementation and stacking produce clipped, conflicting modal states.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found visible role=dialog divs and several iframes; the detail mobile screenshot shows the consent panel wider than the viewport while a second prompt competes for focus.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one correctly sized native dialog for necessary modal consent and a non-modal, user-triggered popover for optional notifications; manage focus and light-dismiss declaratively.

findings.summary: Content is buried under repetitive navigation and very long SEO-oriented copy.
findings.evidence: The homepage probe counted 948 links and 23 site-authored H2 headings before consent-provider headings; the document is about 15,000px tall and the Latest Jobs page about 173,000px tall.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise current jobs/results, deduplicate repeated links and headings, and move secondary explanatory material behind clearly labelled sections.

findings.summary: The representative job detail does not reflow on mobile.
findings.evidence: At 360px, layout evidence reports scrollWidth 663px and 303px horizontal overflow; the clipped table and consent controls are visible in the screenshot.
findings.suggestedFix: Make data tables and overlays intrinsically responsive: use minmax()/grid, overflow wrappers for true tabular data, max-inline-size:100%, and logical spacing.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated on primary controls.
findings.evidence: The focus probe reports outline-style none for navigation links, the logo, search input and skip link after programmatic focus.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible indicator with sufficient offset; do not remove native outlines without an equivalent.

findings.summary: The primary route-to-application journey is blocked at entry.
findings.evidence: Across homepage, listing, detail and contact captures, consent or notification UI covers the next useful action; the detail capture cannot expose the Apply Online control in its first viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Let users read and navigate before optional prompts, surface the official application link prominently, and reserve interruptions for contextual moments.

findings.summary: Unknown URLs do not produce an honest, recoverable not-found state.
findings.evidence: A request to /404-audit-probe/ returned HTTP 301 to the homepage, and the resulting screenshot provides no “not found” explanation or recovery choices.
findings.suggestedFix: Return HTTP 404 with a concise explanation, search, and links to Latest Jobs, Results and Admit Cards.

findings.summary: Load performance and visual stability miss Core Web Vitals targets.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 6.0s and CLS 0.312 (performance 61); mobile layout measured CLS 0.313 on home and 0.481 on detail. The trace recorded 512ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve prompt/ad slots, remove late layout injection, prioritise the real LCP element, and delay non-essential scripts until after content is stable.

findings.summary: Third-party and unused JavaScript dominate the load.
findings.evidence: HAR shows 780KB transferred, 557KB third-party and 590KB script; Lighthouse estimates 241KB unused JavaScript and 14KB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the on-load push SDK, load advertising only after consent and idle time, audit vendor necessity, and split/defer non-critical code.

findings.summary: Automated and DOM evidence shows multiple accessibility failures.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility is 85 and fails colour contrast (9 nodes), iframe title, heading order, link name, and links distinguished only by colour (11 nodes); the search probe also found an unlabelled search input.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix names and labels, title all meaningful iframes, restore sequential headings, underline text links, and update colours to WCAG contrast minimums.

findings.summary: The declared sitemap endpoint is not a sitemap.
findings.evidence: robots.txt advertises /sitemap.xml, but fetching it returned a 164KB HTML homepage with no <urlset> or sitemap index.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a valid XML sitemap at the advertised URL and keep robots.txt, canonical URLs and sitemap entries consistent.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but baseline browser security policies and cookie flags are absent.
findings.evidence: The header audit found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, framing, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy. FCCDCF is not Secure, SameSite=None and lasts 390 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, strict referrer and minimal permissions policy; set Secure and an appropriate SameSite value on cookies.

findings.summary: The default load has a large advertising and consent-vendor privacy footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 7 third-party origins and Google Ads; HAR attributes 19 requests and 557KB to third parties. The rendered consent UI enumerates about 210 partners and precise-geolocation processing.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce vendors to those demonstrably necessary, do not contact advertising origins before consent, and batch/minimise analytics.

findings.summary: Notification permission is solicited without user context.
findings.evidence: Every first-load screenshot shows “want to notify you” with Allow/Deny before the user has requested alerts, stacked over consent.
findings.suggestedFix: Ask for notification permission only after an explicit “Get alerts” action and explain the value and frequency before invoking the browser permission flow.

findings.summary: Runtime overlays are not resilient to narrow viewports.
findings.evidence: On the 360px detail page, the consent dialog starts at x=76 and extends well beyond the right edge; key controls and text are clipped.
findings.suggestedFix: Constrain top-layer UI with max-inline-size:calc(100dvi - 2rem), logical margins and overflow handling, and test nested prompts at narrow widths.

findings.summary: Mixed English/Hindi content is not marked for language changes.
findings.evidence: The document declares only lang=en-US while the title/description and visible content include Hindi text; no element-level Hindi language metadata was observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Use the correct primary language and wrap language changes with lang="hi" (and appropriate script/dir metadata where needed); prefer logical CSS properties.

findings.summary: Asset delivery and image sizing still waste bytes.
findings.evidence: Image evidence found one missing-dimension image, one oversized logo, two images without srcset and one below-fold image not lazy-loaded; Lighthouse reports image-delivery and cache-lifetime savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve correctly sized responsive images with width/height and srcset/sizes, lazy-load below-fold imagery, and apply long immutable caching to versioned assets.

findings.summary: Route and attention changes are abrupt on a long multi-page experience.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no authored view-transition or scroll-state rules; the listing template is roughly 173,000px tall without position feedback.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document View Transitions and a lightweight scroll-progress/current-section cue, respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: Platform hygiene is weakened by missing source maps and an on-load permission prompt.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports missing source maps for a large first-party script; screenshots directly show an unsolicited notification prompt at load.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish correct production source maps to authorised tooling and move permission requests behind explicit user actions.

findings.summary: Dense tables and heading misuse harm reading and assistive navigation.
findings.evidence: The detail probe found two layout tables with 21 rows and zero <th> cells, plus action labels split into repeated H2 “Click Here” headings; at mobile width the table overflows.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic table headers/captions, meaningful link text in the same cell, comfortable line length and responsive table presentation.

findings.summary: The app-like install surface has no content offline strategy.
findings.evidence: A manifest exists and the only active service worker is firebase-messaging-sw.js; no content-caching/offline worker was registered. The manifest also labels a .webp icon as image/png.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a minimal offline fallback/content cache if installability is intentional, or remove the app manifest; correct icon MIME metadata.
